description.en: An OWL ontology and RDF knowledge graph harmonising 207 governance requirements drawn from the TCD REAMS research-ethics process, the EU AI Act, Horizon Europe ethics guidance, and the ACM/NeurIPS professional codes, mapped to the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and linked to documented AI-incident precedents. Developed as part of an MSc dissertation at Trinity College Dublin.

comments.en: Ontology for multi-framework AI ethics compliance assessment

comment.undefined: A document or artefact that demonstrates compliance with an ethics requirement.
Everyone who has been charged shall be presumed innocent until proved guilty according to law.
A governance or regulatory framework defining ethics requirements for AI research.

Classification of a requirement by its conditionality. Tier 1 requirements are mandatory for all research proposals. Tier 2 requirements are reflective prompts that apply conditionally based on research context.
A document identifying and evaluating potential harms arising from a research project or AI system.
Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European Parliament and of the Council on Artificial Intelligence. FRIA requirements from Article 27.
A procedure for evaluating the environmental consequences of a research project or AI system deployment.
A documented real-world event in which an AI system caused or contributed to harm, rights violations, or ethical failures.
Risk of mental distress, manipulation, coercion, or emotional damage caused by an AI system.
Everyone has the right to respect for his or her physical and mental integrity.
Risk that AI system design exploits psychological vulnerabilities to create compulsive usage patterns.

label.undefined: Article 31 — Fair and Just Working Conditions

comment.undefined: Every worker has the right to working conditions which respect his or her health, safety and dignity.
A structured procedure for assessing AI system impacts on fundamental rights, aligned with EU AI Act Article 27.
A document through which research participants provide informed consent to participate.
An ethics requirement specifying an action that must be performed. Aligned with ODRL Duty.

label.undefined: Article 47 — Right to an Effective Remedy

comment.undefined: Everyone whose rights and freedoms guaranteed by the law of the Union are violated has the right to an effective remedy before a tribunal.
Risk of chilling, suppressing, or misrepresenting legitimate expression through AI content systems.
European Commission ethics requirements for Horizon Europe funded research projects.
Risk arising from inadequate data stewardship, provenance, or quality controls in AI pipelines.
Everyone has the right to freedom of expression. This right shall include freedom to hold opinions and to receive and impart information and ideas without interference by public authority.
A formal certificate demonstrating completion of a required training or qualification.
Trinity College Dublin Research Ethics Application Management System. Institutional ethics framework for research approval.
Risk that an AI system is used beyond its originally defined and ethically approved purpose.
A category of harm or risk that an AI system may cause to individuals, groups, or society.
No one shall be held in slavery or servitude.

label.undefined: Article 26 — Integration of Persons with Disabilities

comment.undefined: The Union recognises and respects the right of persons with disabilities to benefit from measures designed to ensure their independence, social and occupational integration and participation in the life of the community.
Everyone has the right to life.
The requirement does not apply to this research project given its specific context and scope.
The requirement is fully satisfied by the research project.
A technical or organisational measure that reduces the likelihood or severity of an identified risk.
Risk of economic loss, fraudulent debt, or material deprivation caused by an AI system.
A structured document providing transparency about an AI model's intended uses, performance characteristics, and limitations.
Human dignity is inviolable. It must be respected and protected.
EU Charter Title V covering Articles 39–46 on citizens' rights.

label.undefined: Article 16 — Freedom to Conduct a Business

comment.undefined: The freedom to conduct a business in accordance with Union law and national laws and practices is recognised.
A researcher-completed assessment of the ethical implications of a proposed research project.
Risk that an AI system's operation, capabilities, limitations, or decision rationale are not adequately disclosed to end-users and stakeholders.
An organisational policy documenting how personal data is collected, stored, and processed in compliance with GDPR.
Risk of unauthorised collection, processing, or disclosure of personal data by an AI system.
EU Charter of Fundamental Rights Title I covering Articles 1–5 on human dignity.
Everyone has the right of access to preventive health care and the right to benefit from medical treatment under the conditions established by national laws and practices.
Research ethics and broader impact requirements from ACM, NeurIPS, FAccT, AAAI, and ACL Rolling Review conference submission guidelines.
A systematic evaluation of bias in AI training data, model outputs, or decision processes.
Risk of unfair exclusion, surveillance, or adverse treatment of workers or job applicants by AI systems.
EU Charter Title II covering Articles 6–19 on freedoms.
Risk that an AI system covertly influences behaviour, beliefs, or choices without adequate disclosure or consent.
Union policies shall ensure a high level of consumer protection.

label.undefined: EU Charter of Fundamental Rights Article

comment.undefined: A fundamental right protected under the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union (2000/C 364/01).
EU Charter Title VI covering Articles 47–50 on justice.
EU Charter Title IV covering Articles 27–38 on solidarity and social rights.
Requirements that apply to all research proposals regardless of context. Failure to comply blocks ethics approval.
An ethics requirement specifying an action that is permitted under defined conditions. Aligned with ODRL Permission.

label.undefined: Article 15 — Freedom to Choose an Occupation and Right to Engage in Work

comment.undefined: Everyone has the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion.
Everyone is equal before the law.

label.undefined: Article 7 — Respect for Private and Family Life

comment.undefined: Everyone has the right to respect for his or her private and family life, home and communications.
Risk of unfair differential treatment of individuals or groups based on protected characteristics by an AI system.
Risk of harm to workers arising from AI system deployment in occupational settings.
Risk of undermining democratic institutions, electoral processes, or civic participation through AI systems.
Everyone has the right to the protection of personal data concerning him or her.
A high level of environmental protection and the improvement of the quality of the environment must be integrated into the policies of the Union.
Risk of unauthorised use or infringement of intellectual property in AI training or outputs.
The requirement is not satisfied and remediation is required before ethics approval.
Risk that an AI system misleads users about its nature, capabilities, or the provenance of its outputs.
A formal process for identifying, analysing, and evaluating risks posed by a research project or AI system.
Risk of damage to an individual's or organisation's reputation through AI-generated outputs or decisions.
EU Charter Title III covering Articles 20–26 on equality.
Risk of unjustified restriction of personal liberty through AI-informed decisions (detention, exclusion, coercion).
Risk of systemic or population-level economic disadvantage caused by AI systems (distinct from individual FinancialHarm).
Risk of unauthorised access to or leakage of personal data held or processed by an AI system.
An ethics requirement that forbids a specific action. Aligned with ODRL Prohibition.
Risk of degrading, objectifying, or otherwise undermining human dignity through AI system design or use.

Any discrimination based on any ground such as sex, race, colour, ethnic or social origin, genetic features, language, religion or belief, political or any other opinion, membership of a national minority, property, birth, disability, age or sexual orientation shall be prohibited.
The requirement is partially satisfied but gaps remain that must be addressed.
An assessment evaluating the impact of an AI system on fundamental rights, as referenced in EU AI Act Article 27.
A normative statement derived from a governance framework specifying what a researcher must, may, or must not do.

label.undefined: Article 13 — Freedom of the Arts and Sciences

comment.undefined: The Union recognises and respects the rights of the elderly to lead a life of dignity and independence.
Risk of bodily injury, death, or physical safety compromise caused by an AI system.

label.undefined: Article 12 — Freedom of Assembly and of Association

comment.undefined: Everyone has the right to freedom of peaceful assembly and to freedom of association at all levels, in particular in political, trade union and civic matters, which includes the right of everyone to form and to join trade unions for the protection of his or her interests.
The compliance state of a requirement within a given research project assessment.
A document evaluating the presence and extent of bias in an AI system's training data or outputs.
Risk of gender-based disadvantage, stereotyping, or exclusion produced or amplified by an AI system.
Risk of harm to children's rights, development, or best interests arising from AI systems affecting minors.

label.undefined: Article 23 — Equality Between Women and Men

comment.undefined: Equality between women and men must be ensured in all areas, including employment, work and pay.
Risk of negative environmental impact including carbon footprint, resource consumption, or ecological damage from AI systems.
A formal procedure for evaluating ethics compliance, risk, or impact of a research project or AI system.
Risk that research or AI outputs intended for beneficial purposes are repurposed for harmful applications.
A structured procedure for assessing data protection risks under GDPR Article 35.
Children shall have the right to such protection and care as is necessary for their well-being.
An individual or organisational role involved in the research ethics assessment process.
The Union shall respect cultural, religious and linguistic diversity.
A formal decision by an ethics committee approving a research project to proceed.
Requirements that apply conditionally based on research context. Researchers must reflect on whether these apply to their specific project.
Risk of pervasive or disproportionate observation, tracking, or monitoring of individuals by an AI system.
Risk of incorrect identity attribution (e.g. facial-recognition false matches) with consequential harm.
Every person has the right to have his or her affairs handled impartially, fairly and within a reasonable time by the institutions and bodies of the Union.
A classification of personal or research data relevant to ethics assessment, aligned with GDPR data categories.
A structured document describing the composition, collection process, and intended uses of a dataset.
A systematic assessment of the privacy risks posed by a data processing activity, required under GDPR Article 35.

label.undefined: Article 6 — Right to Liberty and Security

comment.undefined: Everyone has the right to liberty and security of person.
Risk that affected persons cannot obtain explanation, contestation, or remedy for AI-mediated decisions.
